name: col_nchar
title: Count number of characters in an ANSI colored string

origin.description: Count characters after ANSI sequences are removed.

arguments.text: Passed to nchar() after the styles are stripped.

origin.details: This is nchar(strip_style(x), ...). The ANSI bytes are not part of the count.
origin.example:
str <- paste(red("red"), "default", green("green"))
cat(col_nchar(str), "\n", sep="")
cat(nchar(strip_style(str)), "\n", sep="")

translation.description: Count characters after ANSI sequences are removed.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: chars or width use the Python string length. bytes uses the UTF-8 length.

translation.details: The count is taken after strip_style. For the ASCII text in the manual, chars and width agree.
translation.value: An int, or a list of ints.
translation.example:
text = red("red") + " default " + green("green")
print(col_nchar(text))
print(len(strip_style(text)))
